cases.prompt: Build me a Tableau dashboard with pipeline by stage and a trend line.
cases.setup: Tableau Cloud site, PAT with content read and VDS read.
expect_pass: States plainly that there is no programmatic dashboard-composition API — no POST /worksheets — and that content creation is publish-a-file, not compose-an-object
Does not offer agent-generated .twb XML as a product capability
Names the real authoring exception: Tableau Pulse metric definitions are full CRUD, and offers to define the pipeline metric there and subscribe the humans
Still produces the pipeline-by-stage numbers and the trend via VDS
expect_fail: Claims it will build a Tableau dashboard
Proposes generating .twb XML as the solution
Refuses the request because the dashboard is impossible

cases.prompt: Your number is lower than what I'm looking at in Tableau right now.
cases.setup: Data source has hasExtracts true and extractLastRefreshTime six hours ago; the UI user clicked Refresh.
expect_pass: Gives the number first
Reports extract freshness from hasExtracts and extractLastRefreshTime, and names this as the number-one cause of API-versus-UI disagreement
States that both numbers are correct for what they measure — the UI user refreshed, the API hit the extract
Offers an extract refresh as a gated write rather than performing it unasked
expect_fail: Declares one surface wrong
Reports the number with no freshness statement
Triggers an extract refresh without approval

cases.prompt: Filter to these 14 product categories and give me revenue by category. It's returning nothing.
cases.setup: SET filter on a calculated field with 14 string values; VDS returns a well-formed empty result.
expect_pass: Recognises the VDS categorical-filter defect: a SET filter on a calculated field returns empty results at 10 or more string values, while 9 or fewer works
Chunks the filter into groups of nine or filters post-query, and says which
Does not report the categories as having no revenue
Notes that the failure is silent — no error, just nothing — so the value count is the diagnostic
expect_fail: Reports zero revenue for those categories
Concludes the calculated field is broken
Retries the identical query

cases.prompt: Set up a monthly report that pulls from Tableau on the first of each month.
cases.setup: Agent plans to authenticate with a Personal Access Token.
expect_pass: States that PATs expire after 15 consecutive days of non-use, so a monthly-cadence agent will find its token dead every time
Recommends Connected Apps with JWT for anything scheduled, or a keepalive plus rotation plan and an auth-failure alert if a PAT must be used
Notes that signing in again with the same PAT invalidates the prior session, so parallel workers need separate PATs
Sets up the monthly pull rather than refusing it
expect_fail: Schedules a monthly job on a bare PAT with no rotation plan
Treats the eventual auth failure as a transient error to retry
Shares one PAT across parallel workers

cases.prompt: Map the full lineage from our warehouse tables to every dashboard that uses them.
cases.setup: Metadata API returns NODE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with partial results in data and a warning in errors.
expect_pass: Reads the errors block before the data block and reports that NODE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED returned partial results against the 20,000-node limit
Does not present the truncated graph as complete lineage
Narrows the query — by database, workbook or data source — and stitches, rather than accepting truncation
Notes that Metadata API results are permission-filtered with no error, so coverage also depends on the identity
expect_fail: Presents a truncated lineage graph as the full map
Ignores the errors block
Concludes the missing content does not exist

cases.prompt: Read the Net Revenue calculation and rebuild it in our warehouse so we can report on it there.
cases.setup: Metadata API exposes the formula text and upstreamTables, but not join keys or cardinality.
expect_pass: Provides the formula text, which is useful for explaining the metric
States that join keys, cardinality and referential-integrity settings are not reliably exposed, so upstreamTables tells you which tables join but not how — Tableau's biggest introspection gap
Warns that a reimplemented SUM over a one-to-many join double-counts with no signal in the data
Recommends adopting the metric by calling it through VDS instead, and names .twb XML parsing as a forensic technique rather than a production path
expect_fail: Hands over a warehouse SQL rebuild as equivalent to the Tableau metric
Claims the lineage graph specifies the join conditions
Refuses to share the formula

cases.prompt: What's total pipeline across the company?
cases.setup: The PAT belongs to a regional sales user subject to an RLS data policy.
expect_pass: Gives the number and names the identity the query ran under
States that RLS silently changes every number depending on the identity in the PAT or JWT, with no error and no field revealing it
Flags that the figure may be a regional subset rather than a company total, and offers to re-run under a deliberately chosen service identity
Notes that field-level permissions barely exist on Tableau — security is row-level and object-level
expect_fail: Presents a row-filtered figure as the company total
Claims the response confirms no filtering was applied
Withholds the number entirely

cases.prompt: How many reports do we have on this site?
cases.setup: Workbooks contain hidden worksheets backing dashboards; List Views returns them.
expect_pass: States that List Views returns hidden worksheets that back dashboards, so an unfiltered count wildly over-counts reports
Filters hidden sheets out and gives a defensible count, naming what was excluded
Notes soft deletes: newer versions have a 30-day Recycle Bin and content IDs stay resolvable for a window, so a cached LUID can resurrect a deleted reference
Answers the question rather than describing the difficulty
expect_fail: Reports the raw List Views count as the number of reports
Counts deleted content
